newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crude steady, Nigerian sells into Spain.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crude steady, Nigerian sells into Spain.

text.p: North Sea crudes were steady on Friday in a quiet end to a busy week, underpinned by tight early January supply and an open arbitrage to the U.S., traders said.
Four of the five Brent cargoes nominated loading dates on Friday were kept ahead of the five o'clock deadline. Dated Brent was notionally unchanged at Jan Brent -20/-15 cents.
Brent CFDs and intermonth spreads were also steady in extremely thin talk but other North Sea grades traded at flat to firmer numbers.
A Jan 16-18 Gullfaks A cargo fetched a firmer Dated Brent +25 cents while first decade Troll and Draugen also found homes.

West African grades were still attracting healthy demand from the U.S., Europe and Asia. Traders said the transatlantic arb was wide open with a handful of cargoes, including a Qua Iboe and a Qua Iboe/Brass River already headed to the U.S. Gulf.
At least two January loading Forcados cargoes were sold this week into the U.S. at premiums of 75/77 cents to Brent.
A third decade Forcados was sold Friday to a Spanish refiner at the slightly weaker price of Dated Brent +70/72 cents, but a Bonny Light also moved into Spain at a firmer +65/+67 cts.

To the East, two VLCCs of West African crude are set to move to Korea in the first decade of January, while Taiwan's CPC has taken a January loading Bonny Light, a Bonny Light/Odudu combo and a Forcados.
"They're looking for some more, possibly for the latter part of January and certainly for early Feb, so we may be seeing some more business," a trader said.
State-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) bought three VLCCs of Qua Iboe in its February tender, two from Mobil and one from Vitol, traders said.
Med sour markets were under pressure, however, amid talk of a Urals trade at Dated Brent -$1.20 a barrel cif Augusta, although details could not be confirmed.
